title: Cretan Honey & Wine Experience
tagline: A beekeeper's farm, a family winery and five Cretan labels
seoTitle: Cretan Honey & Wine Tasting Tour from Rethymno | Way to Crete
seoDescription: Taste carob, pine and thyme honey with rakomelo and cheese, then five wines at a family winery in Patsos. A 5-6 hour day from Rethymno, pick-up included.
summary: The Cretan Honey & Wine Experience is a 5-6 hour day from Rethymno that pairs a beekeeper's farm with a family-owned winery. Pick-up from your accommodation is at 09:30. At the apiary you taste three honeys - carob, pine and thyme - alongside rakomelo and local cheese; in the green valley of Patsos a small family winery takes you through the vineyard and the production area before a tasting of five Cretan labels; and the day closes over coffee at Gidospito, beside the Potamon Dam. It runs Monday to Friday for up to eight guests, is rated easy, includes a professional photoshoot, and is quoted on request.
overview:
This is a producer day rather than a restaurant day. Crete's food culture is built on a handful of things done well for a very long time - honey, cheese, wine - and the point of this experience is to taste them where they are made and to meet the people who make them.

The first stop is a beekeeper's farm at Lampini. You taste three distinct varieties of Cretan honey: carob, pine and thyme, each with its own aroma and weight on the palate. The tasting continues with rakomelo, the traditional honey-based spirit, and with local cheese served alongside honey, which is the pairing most guests remember: creamy and sweet at once, simple and unexpectedly good.

From there the road climbs into Patsos, a green, well-watered part of inland Rethymno with a long winemaking tradition. The winery is small and family-owned. The visit starts with a guided walk through the vineyard, covering the indigenous grape varieties, what the Cretan climate does to them and the cultivation methods the family has inherited. Inside, you see the production area and the full process, from harvest and fermentation through ageing and bottling, before the tasting itself: five different labels, chosen to show the range of local wine, each explained as you go.

The day ends at Gidospito, near the Potamon Dam, over a traditional coffee and a view of the water and the hills. Transport is by air-conditioned minivan with an English-speaking driver, and an optional guide can be added for an extra fee.

itinerary.heading: 09:30 - pick-up from your accommodation
itinerary.body: We collect you by air-conditioned minivan and drive inland from the Rethymno coast towards the villages of the interior. The driver speaks English; an optional guide can be arranged in advance for an additional fee.

itinerary.heading: Honey tasting at the beekeeper's farm
itinerary.body: At a beekeeper's farm in Lampini you are introduced to Cretan honey and taste three varieties - carob, pine and thyme - each carrying the scent of a different part of the landscape and a different season. The tasting also takes in rakomelo, the traditional honey-based spirit, and local cheese paired with honey.

itinerary.heading: Vineyard walk and winery visit in Patsos
itinerary.body: In the lush area of Patsos we visit a small, family-owned winery. The visit begins outside with a guided walk through the vineyard, covering the indigenous grape varieties, the influence of the Cretan climate and the traditional cultivation methods passed down through generations. Inside, you follow the process from harvesting and fermentation to ageing and bottling.

itinerary.heading: Tasting five Cretan wines
itinerary.body: The visit ends with a seated tasting of five different labels, selected to show the diversity and character of Cretan wine. Each is introduced as you taste, so the aromas and flavours make sense in the context of the vineyard you have just walked through.

itinerary.heading: Coffee at Gidospito by the Potamon Dam
itinerary.body: The last stop is Gidospito, near the impressive Potamon Dam, for a traditional coffee in a quiet setting surrounded by water and hills. It is an unhurried end to the day before the drive back to your accommodation.

faqs.a: Three varieties of Cretan honey - carob, pine and thyme - plus rakomelo, the traditional honey-based spirit, and local cheese served with honey. At the winery there is a tasting of five different Cretan labels, and the day ends with a traditional coffee at Gidospito.

faqs.q: How long does the day last and when does it start?
faqs.a: Pick-up from your accommodation is at 09:30 and the experience lasts 5 to 6 hours door to door. It runs Monday to Friday for groups of up to eight guests.

The price includes an English-speaking driver, and the producers themselves lead the honey tasting and the winery visit. A dedicated guide is optional and available for an additional fee - ask for it when you enquire.
No price is published for this experience. We quote on request, based on the size of your group and your pick-up point. Most guests choose to run it as a private experience.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for children or for people who do not drink?
faqs.a: The honey farm, the vineyard walk and the coffee stop suit all ages, and the wine tasting is for adults only. Tell us who is travelling when you enquire and we will confirm the arrangements.
No. The difficulty level is easy. The only walking involved is a gentle stroll through the vineyard and around the farm.
